children: Kainan Holding Group, a British Virgin Islands company operating in Malaysia, filed for an initial public offering on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the symbol “KHG.” The company plans to sell 4,000,000 ordinary shares at an estimated price range of $4.00 to $6.00 per share. D. Boral Capital is the sole underwriter for the offering.

Kainan Holding Group provides one‑stop workforce and human resources management services, focused on sourcing, recruiting, deploying and managing legally employed workers for corporate customers in Malaysia. The company primarily serves manufacturing, construction and service‑based industries, aiming to reduce clients’ administrative burden and improve workforce continuity through structured onboarding, compliance support, attendance tracking and reporting. Revenue is earned over time, typically based on confirmed attendance or hours worked multiplied by agreed pay rates per contract.

Kainan maintains an extensive pool of casual and skilled temporary workers and offers related coordination such as accommodation, transportation and welfare support when included in engagements. The company is investing in systems and processes to scale multi‑site deployments and strengthen data reporting. In addition to its core staffing services, Kainan has been appointed as a panel specialist for water reclamation plant projects (EPCC and O&M) and received a purchase order valued at RM8.33 million, representing a selective expansion of its capabilities into sustainable industrial water infrastructure.
: Malaysia’s construction work value reached RM158.8 billion in 2024, up 20.2% year-over-year; construction represented ~4.1% of GDP (prelim.)
: Double‑digit recovery in construction activity and continued project pipelines support ongoing labor demand
: Provider of outsourced, compliant workforce solutions to manufacturing, construction and services customers across Malaysia
: National, regional and local temporary staffing firms and manpower outsourcing companies

: More complex foreign worker processes (ePPAx/CIMS integration), policy to reduce reliance on foreign labor (Thirteenth Malaysia Plan, multi‑tier levy in 2026), rising adoption of contract staffing, and data center build‑outs driving incremental labor needs
: 92 customers and a managed workforce of 3,498 persons (FY2026); 105 customers and a managed workforce of 3,365 persons (FY2025)
: Services delivered across Malaysia, with principal office in Selangor
: Top customer accounted for ~15% of revenue in FY2026 (26% in FY2025); second-largest customer ~12% in FY2026 (19% in FY2025)
: Foreign workers comprised ~97.11% of deployed workforce in FY2026 (~97.38% in FY2025)
: Appointed panel specialist for water reclamation plants; received RM8,325,050 purchase order in Jan 2026 (project expected to complete by Dec 2026)
: RM8,000,000 in advances to secure specialty equipment and engineering services for the water reclamation project
: CIDB and SPAN‑related requirements noted for construction and water sector projects; ongoing documentation and onboarding controls

, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer - Over 15 years in workforce management in Malaysia; leads strategy, operations and stakeholder relations; expanded company into EPCC and water‑infrastructure projects.
, Chief Financial Officer - More than 9 years in taxation, accounting and financial management; previously with YYC Management Services; oversees budgeting, reporting and internal controls.
, Independent Director Nominee - Corporate and commercial lawyer; experience in restructurings, insolvency and governance; co‑author on Malaysian corporate rescue law.
, Independent Director Nominee - 15+ years in logistics and manufacturing operations; managed warehousing and multi‑site logistics for retail and automotive leather manufacturing.
, Independent Director Nominee - London‑based corporate financier with experience in M&A and capital raising across sectors; founder of J and L Roberts Advisors.
: 40% business expansion and workforce growth; 40% technology, digital infrastructure and systems upgrades; remainder for general corporate purposes and working capital.
